skill.name: copywriting
skill.description: Write conversion-focused landing page and email copy through a confirmed brief, clear structure, honest claims, and testable alternatives.
skill.summary: Create clear, honest, and testable marketing copy from a confirmed copy brief.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All four static findings are false positives caused by generic wording in copywriting guidance. The skill contains no scripts, network operations, prompt injection text, or instructions to access sensitive data.

static_findings.snippet: - Avoid buzzwords unless customers use them
Avoid stacking features without narrative flow.
- Avoid combining multiple messages into one element

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 126 says to avoid buzzwords unless customers use them, which is copywriting style guidance. It does not request system discovery, host details, or environment inspection.
Line 168 advises against stacking features without narrative flow. This is page structure guidance, not an instruction to inspect systems or gather machine information.
Line 211 recommends keeping test messages isolated for A/B testing. The context is marketing copy testing, not system reconnaissance or security probing.
Lines 32-33 contain general copywriting principles about clarity and outcomes. There is no network access, scanning request, endpoint discovery, or data collection instruction.

content.user_title: Write Conversion Copy With Strong Briefs
content.value_statement: Teams often publish copy based on vague assumptions and unsupported claims. This skill builds a confirmed brief before drafting clear landing page or email copy.
actual_capabilities: Collects page purpose, audience, offer, proof, traffic source, and awareness level before drafting.
Creates a copy brief summary and asks for confirmation before writing final copy.
Drafts labeled page sections, including headlines, subheadlines, CTAs, and body copy.
Provides two or three headline and CTA alternatives with brief rationales.
Documents assumptions and explains why key copy choices were made.
Recommends next-step testing when copy is intended for experiments.
limitations: Requires accurate product, audience, and proof inputs from the user.
Does not invent claims, statistics, testimonials, or guarantees.
Does not replace legal, compliance, or brand approval for regulated claims.
Focuses on copy structure, not visual design or page implementation.

use_cases.title: Launch a Landing Page
use_cases.description: Turn a product offer, audience notes, and proof points into a structured landing page draft.

use_cases.title: Improve Campaign Copy
use_cases.description: Create clearer headlines, CTAs, and objection handling for paid, organic, or referral traffic.

use_cases.title: Prepare Copy Tests
use_cases.description: Generate isolated headline and CTA options that can support A/B testing decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Copy Brief
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with basic inputs before any draft is written.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a copy brief for a landing page. Ask for any missing details before writing copy.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Landing Page Copy
prompt_templates.scenario: Use confirmed inputs to produce a structured page draft.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this confirmed brief to write landing page copy with headlines, subheadline, CTA, section copy, and assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Create CTA Alternatives
prompt_templates.scenario: Explore options for a campaign or page section.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate three headline and CTA options for this offer. Include a short rationale for each option.

prompt_templates.title: Refine for Testing
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this page copy for testability. Separate mixed messages, identify assumptions, and suggest next-step A/B tests.

output_examples.input: A founder needs homepage copy for a new workflow automation tool.
output_examples.output: The skill first asks for audience, primary CTA, differentiator, proof, and traffic source. It then prepares a brief for confirmation before drafting.

output_examples.input: A marketing team has a confirmed brief for a trial signup page.
output: Headline: Automate client intake without adding another admin tool.
Subheadline: Turn forms, approvals, and follow-ups into one guided workflow for your operations team.
Primary CTA: Start a guided trial.

output_examples.input: A growth team wants test ideas for a product page headline.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests isolated headline variants based on outcome, pain point, and proof. Each option includes a rationale and testing note.

best_practices: Provide real proof, audience language, and objections before asking for final copy.
Confirm the copy brief before drafting full page or email content.
Keep one goal per page section so messages stay clear and testable.
anti_patterns: Asking for persuasive claims without verified proof or source material.
Combining several audiences, offers, and CTAs into one page brief.
Skipping brief confirmation and requesting final copy from incomplete inputs.

faq.question: Does this skill write full landing pages?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft labeled sections such as headlines, CTAs, body copy, social proof, objections, and final calls to action.

faq.question: Can it write email copy?
faq.answer: Yes. The same brief-first workflow can support campaign and email copy when the offer and audience are clear.

faq.question: Will it create statistics or testimonials?
faq.answer: No. The skill requires real proof and marks missing proof as a placeholder.

faq.question: Does it ask questions before writing?
faq.answer: Yes. It gathers context and asks the user to confirm the copy brief before final drafting.

faq.question: Can it help with A/B tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create isolated headline and CTA options and recommend next-step testing.
